spec.description: Observations from every station in a public forecast zone, over a span, newest first. The same rows `stations.get_observations` returns for each of `stations.list_stations_for_zone`, merged.

start.description: Start of the span, inclusive. The service keeps about a week of observations.

end.description: End of the span, exclusive: an observation at exactly `end` is not returned.

limit.description: Observations per response, newest kept. Range [1, 500].

notes: No `pagination` block, deliberately. A capped response keeps the newest rows (measured 2026-09-30 on WAZ315, 02:00 to 08:00 on 2026-09-29: `limit=10` answers exactly the first ten of the 373 uncapped rows), so the walk would be a `seek` moving `end`. But `timestamp` is not unique here: the zone's six stations report on the same minutes (73 repeated timestamps in those 373 rows), and `end` is exclusive (`end=07:53:00Z` answers 07:50 rows, `end=07:53:01Z` 07:53 rows). A walk moving an exclusive `end` to a shared minute would skip that minute's unread rows, so no walk is declared rather than a lossy one. For a long span, walk `stations.get_observations_paged` per station.
The `pagination.next` the service sends is not this endpoint's: it is a `/stations/<first station>/observations?cursor=...` URL.
